heading: Best Sushi in Kelowna
title: Best Sushi in Kelowna | Okanagan Roam
description: Where to eat sushi in Kelowna: a tiny chef's counter, late-night rolls, all-you-can-eat, sashimi bento lunches, vegan sushi bowls and izakaya plates.
intro: Kelowna has more sushi than you might expect for a lake town. This guide sorts it by the kind of meal you want: a seat at a chef's counter, a dependable neighbourhood spot, a cheap pile of rolls, a quick casual bite, or an izakaya night with ramen and skewers.

Most picks are in Kelowna, from downtown and Pandosy to the Mission, Glenmore and Rutland. A few are across the bridge in West Kelowna and up the highway in Lake Country. For more of the city, see our {page:/kelowna/restaurants|Kelowna restaurants} page.

sections.heading: Chef's counters & a night out
sections.lead: For when the meal is the evening's plan.

items.name: SUSHI HAYASHI
items.text: a tiny counter where you watch the chef work up close, which is half the draw. The sushi tower and the katsu both get specific praise.

items.name: Wa Skew'r Sushi & Bar
items.text: a Japanese izakaya that goes a step past the usual sushi menu. Order skewers and sashimi, then work through the sake list.

items.name: Bluetail Sushi - Commerce
items.text: dim lighting, a late-night crowd and experimental rolls for anyone ready to skip the California roll. Start with the beef tataki.

items.name: Momo Sushi Mission
items.text: creative special rolls are the reason to come, so order one of those over the usual. Attentive tea service runs through the meal.

sections.heading: Neighbourhood sushi bars
sections.lead: Smaller, steady places that regulars return to.

items.name: Aomi Sushi Japanese Restaurant
items.text: an unassuming Lower Mission spot where the yakiudon and sashimi have always been the strengths. On a first visit, order what the regulars trust.

items.name: Yama Kitchen
items.text: a locally owned sushi spot that regulars praise for consistent quality. Go at lunch for the generous sashimi bento.

items.name: Mizu Japanese Restaurant
items.text: handmade Japanese food on Pandosy Street since 2000, now under new owners. A casual spot for a family meal, with generous rolls and easy parking.

items.name: Mabui Kitchen
items.text: a cozy Mission-area spot with a loyal following for its distinctive menu. Order the temaki, and don't skip the cream soda float.

sections.heading: All-you-can-eat & value
sections.lead: Rolls that won't stretch the budget.

items.name: Tokyo 1
items.text: the city's only all-you-can-eat Japanese restaurant. You order on a tablet, and the dining room feels upscale for the price.

items.name: Maki Sushi Restaurant
items.text: a cozy, homey room on Harvey Ave with reasonable prices and a tofu-friendly menu. The dancing eel and Kelowna maki rolls are the specialties.

items.name: Misato's Kitchen
items.text: a wood-panelled spot on Ellis St that stays open late after other kitchens close. The rolls are cheap, and the salmon sashimi comes thick and fatty.

items.name: Yuzu Bowl and Bistro
items.text: a Japanese bistro that welcomes kids. Time your visit for the happy hour roll deal.

sections.heading: Quick & casual
sections.lead: Easy weeknight sushi, and one for plant-based eaters.

items.name: Dozo House
items.text: a casual spot in Glenmore's Kane Road plaza for sushi, ramen, tempura and bento boxes. Reviewers mention quick, friendly service and good value.

items.name: OKA Japanese Restaurant
items.text: a family-friendly room in Orchard Plaza on Cooper Road, with sushi rolls, tempura and chicken karaage. Reviewers mention quick service.

items.name: Naked Cafe
items.text: a dedicated vegan cafe and a longtime favourite for plant-based eating. Its name was made on the sushi bowls and the Japanese curry.

sections.heading: Across the bridge & up the highway
sections.lead: Worth the short drive from downtown Kelowna. Our {page:/guides/best-restaurants-west-kelowna|West Kelowna restaurants guide} has more on that side of the lake.

items.name: Asuki sushi
items.text: a newer spot with creative, generously portioned rolls at reasonable prices. Order something you wouldn't normally try.

items.name: Ginza Sushi West Kelowna
items.text: consistent, budget-friendly sushi rather than a special-occasion spot. Reviewers point to the yam roll and miso soup combination.

items.name: Turtle Bay GOGO Sushi
items.text: a sushi spot in Winfield that locals say is worth the detour.

sections.heading: Beyond sushi: ramen & izakaya
sections.lead: For a bowl of broth or a group night out. Our {page:/guides/soup-ramen-pho-okanagan|soup, ramen and pho guide} has more ramen across the valley.

items.name: O-Zeki Japanese Restaurant
items.text: private tatami-style booths suit a group. Book one and order the group platters and the tonkotsu ramen.

items.name: Wasabi Ramen and Izakaya
items.text: tucked off Bernard Ave, with a quiet, devoted following. Order the okonomiyaki and one of the rich ramen broths.
